record.original_question: Consider a Poisson manifold M of even dimension such that it is symplectic on a dense set U ⊂ M. Assume that M is endowed with a toric action which is Hamiltonian on U. Is there an analog of Delzant theorem for the image of the moment map? 34 Furthermore, in view of [168] where the Moser homotopy method is p resented also for foliated mani- folds, can Delzant theorem be generalised for regular Poisson manif olds? We conclude this section with a problem related to the symplectic case. However, its solution might require some Poisson techniques. There are two obstructions to g lobalizing action-angle coordinates, as described by Duistermaat [68]: the Hamiltonian monodromy and the Chern (or Duistermaat-Chern) class. Contrary to the former, the latter has been very little inves tigated. There are, clearly, at least two reasons for this: • The Chern class always vanishes for two degrees of freedom syste ms; • There are no known physically meaningful examples with non-trivial C hern class in three degrees of freedom. Although it is easy to manually construct any Chern class, see [8], hav ing a natural example from classical mechanics would provide better motivation for further st udy (see also Problem 7.4).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a Poisson manifold of even dimension, and let $U \subset M$ be a dense open subset on which the Poisson structure is nondegenerate (so $(U,\omega)$ is symplectic). Suppose an $n$-torus $T^n$ (with $\dim M = 2n$) acts effectively on $M$, and that the restricted action on $U$ is Hamiltonian with moment map $\mu : U \to \mathfrak{t}^*$ which extends continuously to $M$.

(a) Formulate and prove an analogue of the Delzant classification theorem in this setting: determine to what extent the image $\mu(M) \subset \mathfrak{t}^*$ (together with appropriate combinatorial data on its boundary, reflecting the locus where the Poisson structure degenerates) is a complete invariant of $(M,\pi,T^n\text{-action})$ up to equivariant Poisson isomorphism, and characterize which subsets of $\mathfrak{t}^*$ arise as such moment-map images.

(b) More generally, let $(M,\pi)$ be a regular Poisson manifold (the symplectic foliation has constant rank) endowed with an effective Hamiltonian torus action of dimension equal to half the leaf dimension. Generalize the Delzant classification theorem to this regular Poisson setting, classifying such Hamiltonian toric regular Poisson manifolds by suitable polytopal/combinatorial data on the leaf space.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist. The case of toric log symplectic manifolds (where the Poisson structure degenerates along a hypersurface) was classified via a "tropical momentum map" by Gualtieri–Li–Pelayo–Ratiu (2014). Classification of multiplicity-free Hamiltonian actions by regular proper symplectic groupoids in the regular Poisson setting was carried out more recently (e.g., Crainic–Fernandes–Martínez-Torres, 2024). A fully general Delzant-type theorem for arbitrary Poisson manifolds symplectic on a dense set, or for arbitrary regular Poisson manifolds, does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: The tropical momentum map: a classification of toric log symplectic manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of toric log symplectic manifolds via a tropical momentum map, an analog of Delzant in a Poisson setting where M is symplectic off a hypersurface.
status_evidence.claim: A Delzant-type classification exists for toric log symplectic manifolds, a special case of Poisson manifolds symplectic on a dense set.

status_evidence.title: On the classification of multiplicity-free Hamiltonian actions by regular proper symplectic groupoids
status_evidence.snippet: Natural generalization of symplectic toric manifolds in the context of regular Poisson manifolds of compact types; classification in terms of Delzant subspaces of the orbit space.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward a Delzant theorem for regular Poisson manifolds via symplectic groupoid techniques.
